findings.title: ARTEX and Friends: Enter Agentic Offensive Frameworks
findings.summary_md: Google Threat Intelligence Group and Mandiant reported observing ARTEX, HexStrike, CAIRN and PentAGI in incident-response engagements, with agentic activity covering lateral movement, database exploitation and preparation for exfiltration. They described ARTEX sequences running in roughly two-to-25-second bursts, including 27 events in 23 seconds, and probe artifacts using the `artex-probe-*` filename pattern. The report said the observed intrusions still relied on familiar weaknesses such as compromised credentials and unpatched systems, but automated chaining increased their speed and scale.

findings.title: ARTEX and AI-Powered Red Teaming Tools: What Defenders Need to Know
findings.summary_md: Unit 42 identified 1,323 internet-facing hosts running CyberStrikeAI and 609 running ARTEX as of October 2026, with 21 running both. It reported observed intrusions in which attackers used public password-reset pages and exposed APIs to reach cloud environments without exploiting a software vulnerability. The report describes bursts of one to 14 requests about a second apart, pauses of 25 to 31 seconds, and pivots within about a minute of a credential download, recommending behavioral hunts for canary usernames, new cloud-key source IPs and write-then-delete storage tests.

findings.title: Inside the loop: Five AI attack frameworks that never ask permission
findings.summary_md: Elastic compared ARTEX, CyberStrikeAI, Cairn, PentAGI and HexStrike, reporting that all five had appeared in intrusions and describing ARTEX activity in two-to-25-second bursts. It said none of the five enforced authorization in code by default and presented an ES|QL hunt for request tempo, tool-family diversity and sequences across web, proxy and cloud audit logs. It warned that source-address and framework fingerprints age quickly because agents rotate infrastructure and change tools.

findings.title: Cyberattacks involving AI agents: First confirmed cases in Switzerland
findings.summary_md: Switzerland's National Cyber Security Centre confirmed its first AI-agent-assisted cyberattacks against Swiss organizations and critical-infrastructure operators across at least two sectors. It said the agents could search for vulnerabilities, select tools, evaluate results and plan subsequent attack steps, exploiting standard or easily guessed passwords and known software flaws. The bulletin named ARTEX and CyberStrikeAI as examples of publicly accessible agents and urged reduced internet exposure, critical patching within 24 hours, MFA or passkeys, least privilege and behavioral monitoring.
